extracted.intended_audience: playwrights, poets, and students of poetics/classical literature
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for composing and judging tragic drama (plot, episodes, chorus, diction, thought, and stylistic devices) following Aristotelian poetics. Focuses on structuring action, eliciting pity/fear, diction choices, and integrating chorus and episodes into the whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convincing portrayal of emotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who feel emotion are most convincing through natural sympathy with the characters they represent; one who is agitated storms, one who is angry rages, with the most life-like reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actors/poet should aim for natural, life-like expression of passions; this effect may arise from natural talent or an inspired 'madness' that enables assuming characters. The performer's sympathy with the character creates verisimilitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work out play with appropriate gestures
rubrics_metrics.description: The poet should work out his play, to the best of his power, with appropriate gestures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage action and visible gestures must align with the situation—failure to stage essential physical detail can offend the audience (example: a performance failed because of an 'oversight' in staging).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sketch general outline then fill episodes
rubrics_metrics.description: As for the story...he should first sketch its general outline, and then fill in the episodes and amplify in detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with the overall plan (illustrated by Iphigenia example), then add episodes. The poet need not include incidental causes within the general plan, but episodes must be constructed to serve the plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episodes must be relevant to the action
rubrics_metrics.description: We must see that [episodes] are relevant to the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When adding episodes, ensure they contribute to or connect with the main action (e.g., Orestes' madness and purification relate to the plot). Irrelevant insertions weaken the drama.

rubrics_metrics.name: Episode length: brevity in drama
rubrics_metrics.description: In the drama, the episodes are short, but it is these that give extension to Epic poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep dramatic episodes concise; long episodic expansion suits epic length but not tragic stage economy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish essence of plot and episodic material
rubrics_metrics.description: The essence of the plot is a compact sequence (example: Odyssey core events), the rest is episode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate the minimal causal chain that constitutes the plot from supplementary episodes; focus on the essential events that drive the catastrophe and resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tragedy structure: Complication and Unravelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Every tragedy falls into two parts,—Complication and Unravelling (Désis and Lysis): Complication extends from the beginning to the turning-point to good or bad fortune; Unravelling extends from the beginning of the change to the end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the play so the first part builds to the reversal/turning point and the second resolves consequences to a coherent end (examples: Lynceus of Theodectes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Complex tragedy: reversal and recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: There are four kinds of Tragedy, the Complex, depending entirely on Reversal of the Situation and Recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For complex plots, center structure on peripeteia (reversal) and anagnorisis (recognition) as the main engines of tragic effect and moral satisfaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition must be plausible/natural
rubrics_metrics.description: The mode of recognition may be either that of Euripides or of Polyidus...e.g., a natural exclamation that reveals identity and effects salvation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make recognitions feel emotionally and narratively plausible (the example: a brother's natural exclamation saves him). Avoid contrived or awkward recognitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chorus as integral actor
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chorus too should be regarded as one of the actors; it should be an integral part of the whole, and share in the action, in the manner not of Euripides but of Sophocles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the chorus to participate in and advance the subject matter; avoid choral interludes that are merely ornamental or unrelated (criticized as later poets' practice begun by Agathon).

rubrics_metrics.name: Thought: include proof/refutation and excitation of feelings
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Thought is included every effect which has to be produced by speech, the subdivisions being—proof and refutation; the excitation of the feelings, such as pity, fear, anger, and the like.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose speeches to perform rhetorical functions (demonstration/refutation) and to arouse specific emotions; thought is responsible for preparing pathos (pity, fear, anger) and magnitude where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat dramatic incidents like speeches for emotional effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Dramatic incidents must be treated from the same points of view as dramatic speeches, when the object is to evoke pity, fear, importance, or probability. The only difference is that the incidents should speak for themselves without verbal exposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design incidents so their composition and presentation (action, timing, causality) directly produce the intended emotional responses, rather than relying on explanatory speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modes of expression (diction) belong to delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: One branch of the inquiry treats of the Modes of Expression. But this province of knowledge belongs to the art of Delivery...includes what is a command, a prayer, a narrative, a threat, a question, an answer, and so forth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that fine distinctions of expression type (command vs prayer etc.) are matters of delivery/acting, not strictly of poetic composition; poets are not to be severely censured for such confusions in wording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language taxonomy: parts of speech and phonetics matter to metre
rubrics_metrics.description: Language includes Letter, Syllable, Connecting word, Noun, Verb, Inflexion or Case, Sentence or Phrase; letters and syllables vary (vowel, semi-vowel, mute) and these considerations belong to metrical science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be attentive to phonetic and metrical properties (syllable formation, aspirates, long/short vowels) because they affect metre and sound; detailed technicalities relate to metrical craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metaphor: types and legitimate uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Metaphor is the application of an alien name by transference either from genus to species, or from species to genus, or from species to species, or by analogy/proportion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ metaphors by genus↔species, species↔genus, species↔species, or by proportional analogy; metaphors can be qualified or extended (examples: 'cup of Ares', 'evening as old age of day'). Metaphorical language is a key stylistic device.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word-categories and stylistic palette
rubrics_metrics.description: Every word is either current, or strange, or metaphorical, or ornamental, or newly-coined, or lengthened, or contracted, or altered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a balanced mixture: current words give clarity; strange/metaphorical/ornamental or modified words give elevation and distinction. Examples include newly-coined forms and lengthened/contracted variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perfection of style: clear without being mean
rubrics_metrics.description: The perfection of style is to be clear without being mean. The clearest style is that which uses only current or proper words; at the same time it is mean.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for perspicuity but avoid banal plainness. Combine proper (current) words for clarity with measured use of rare/metaphorical/altered words for loftiness; entirely plain diction can be 'mean' (undesirable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid wholly unusual diction (no riddle or jargon)
rubrics_metrics.description: A style wholly composed of such [unusual] words is either a riddle or a jargon: a riddle, if it consists of metaphors; a jargon, if it consists of strange (or rare) words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not make your diction wholly metaphorical (produces riddles) or wholly strange (produces jargon). A controlled infusion of unusual terms is appropriate; total replacement of common words is harmful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licenses (lengthening, contraction, alteration) can aid clarity and distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: Lengthenings, contractions and alterations of words contribute much to producing a clearness of diction that is remote from commonness...the partial conformity with usage will give perspicuity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ phonetic or morphological licenses in measured cases to gain distinction while retaining enough conventional usage to preserve clarity. Critics who uniformly condemn these licenses are mistaken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderate mixing of dialects, metaphors, and rare forms
rubrics_metrics.description: A certain infusion of strange (or rare) word, the metaphorical, the ornamental, and the other kinds above mentioned, will raise style above the commonplace while the use of proper words will make it perspicuous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blend exotic/dialectal terms and figurative language with familiar idiom to achieve both elevation and intelligibility; avoid over-mixing that produces obscurity or comic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid gratuitous transfers of large passages
rubrics_metrics.description: What difference is there between introducing such choral interludes, and transferring a speech, or even a whole act, from one play to another?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not introduce material (choral interludes, speeches, acts) that are effectively transplanted from other plays without fitting them organically into the present whole; such practice undermines unity.
